content:
incident-bot: [P1] KV-cache reuse error-rate spike on serving-runtime-prod. Metric: kv_reuse_error_rate > 5% for 5m. Affected: continuous-batching path, gpus-asia-2. Suspected stale seq offsets / cross-request values. Playbook: https://redwood/playbooks/kv-cache

Omar Khan: I'm on it. Paging now. Which customers impacted?

Anya Patel: Seeing increased 500s and wrong completions for long-context chat flows. One enterprise tenant (acme-corp) reported hallucinated persona switches. Error logs show "unexpected seq_offset mismatch" and "kv_lookup returned value for different request_id".

Sam Lee: Adding logs snippet:
```
2026-03-02T09:12:45Z ERROR runtime: kv_cache: seq_mismatch: expected 4123 got 4099 request_id=abc123 model=xlarge-8
2026-03-02T09:12:46Z WARN  runtime: kv_reuse: hit stale key owner=worker-7 cache_slot=42
```

Omar Khan: Immediate mitigations: 1) disable kv_reuse_flag on serving runtime (hotpatch), 2) reduce batch_max_size to 4 to limit cross-request mixing, 3) route acme-corp to safe pool.

Anya Patel: How to disable kv_reuse_flag in prod quickly?

Sam Lee: Patch command:
```
kubectl -n serving-runtime patch configmap runtime-config --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/data/kv_reuse_enabled","value":"false"}]'
kubectl rollout restart deployment/serving-runtime
```

oncall-ml: rolled kv_reuse off on cluster gpus-asia-2, patch applied. Watching error rate.

deploy-bot: deploy/runtime-config v2.14.7-hotfix rolled out to gpus-asia-2

Omar Khan: Routing change: patched ingress -> canary routing rule for acme-corp to go to pool-gold-safe. Command:
```
redwood route update --customer acme-corp --pool pool-gold-safe --dry-run=false
```

Katie Wu: Noted. Customer comms draft:
"We're investigating a runtime cache issue causing incorrect outputs for some long-context sessions. We've applied an initial mitigation and routing change; further updates in 30m."

Juan Perez: Also saw memory climb on worker-7 before errors. Could be cache blowup leading to eviction/tombstones and stale keys.

Anya Patel: Error rate dropped to 0.9% after kv_reuse toggle and batch_size reduction. But latency increased ~12ms. We'll keep mitigations until root cause identified.

Sam Lee: Next steps: capture a full pprof from worker-7, dump KV cache contents for analysis (non-prod sanitized), and replay failing requests against current runtime.

oncall-ml: Captured pprof -> https://s3.redwood/profiles/1767456789/worker-7.pprof
KV dump location -> https://s3.redwood/dumps/1767456789/kv-dump-42.json

Omar Khan: Handoff to next oncall @Juan Perez in 40m. Juan please own postmortem and customer follow-up. I'll update incident channel at 10:00.

Juan Perez: Ack. I'll take lead. Will run regression test for seq offsets and try to reproduce with stress harness.

Anya Patel: Flagging related CI test flakiness from last deploy: batching v2 change had a race in slot assignment. Might be root cause.

Sam Lee: Filing postmortem ticket: ENG-INC-4621. Assigning to Juan, Sam, Anya. Include timeline and mitigation notes.

deploy-bot: Hotfix rollback for batching v2 queued (deploy-id: hotfix-20260302-01). Approval by Omar required.

Omar Khan: Approving hotfix rollback. Proceed.

deploy-bot: Rollback complete. Routing and config stable. Monitoring.

Katie Wu: I'll send updated customer note: "We've deployed additional fixes and rolled back a batching change suspected to cause the issue. We're continuing analysis and will share a postmortem." :thumbsup:

oncall-ml: Current status: impact reduced, service stable, incident state -> monitoring. Will transition to postmortem after root-cause confirmed.

Juan Perez: Plan: reproduce with harness, fix sequence assignment race, add KV cache owner tagging + stronger invariants, add e2e test for seq offsets. ETA for patch: 3 days.

Omar Khan: Great. Closing live incident thread when monitoring ok for 2h. Thanks all for quick response. :tada:
